text:
Carla (Support): Hey team, escalation from AcmeCorp — they see p99 latency jump on /v1/generate starting ~09:10 UTC. Previously p99 ~450ms, now reports 3.8s+ and several 5xx user-facing errors. Customer provided repro steps and sample request.

Ben (Infra): Noted. I can see an upward shift in p95/p99 in the per-model dashboard around 09:08 UTC. Looking at traces now.

Alice (SRE): Thanks. Can you paste the trace IDs or a link to the span waterfall?

Ben (Infra): Link: https://observability.internal/redwood/dashboard?query=model:redwood-v1%20latency%20p99

Ben (Infra): Quick summary: tail latencies spiked correlated with a deployment at 09:05 — rollout of redwood-v1@v2026-03-09-2. CPU on GPU nodes stayed normal, but queue wait time and token-generation time increased.

Carla (Support): Customer repro (they included):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","input":"<~3k token prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
They said p99 ~4s, p50 ~600ms. They tried region=us-east-1 and got same.

Alice (SRE): Ok. Two potential vectors: model rollout regressions (changes to attention kernels / token loop) or traffic pattern (a few big requests causing prefix cache churn and longer decode).

Marc (DevOps): I see increased KV cache evictions for the redwood-v1 partition around the same time (metrics: kv_cache_evictions spikes). That would blow up decode work per request.

Lisa (Product): Customer uses batch size 1 on interactive calls. They mentioned a sudden surge of concurrent sessions starting 09:07. Could be a small number of heavy users.

Ben (Infra): Trace snippet (sanitized):
```
span: request.id=abc123 -> wait_in_queue=120ms -> dispatch=20ms -> kv_lookup=2.8s -> decode=900ms -> response
```

Alice (SRE): kv_lookup 2.8s is the culprit. If prefix/KV cache misses balloon, decode cost skyrockets. Immediate mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant circuit breaker to protect platform, 2) enable fallback model variant (redwood-v1-small) for that tenant, 3) temporarily pin to previous model rollout version for all production traffic.

Marc (DevOps): I can flip circuit breaker rules. Recommend aggressive backoff for error/backpressure and strict concurrency per-tenant: concurrency_limit=4, rate_limit=10 rps, token_limit=2048.

Alice (SRE): Do it. Also create a temporary routing rule: if model=redwood-v1 and tenant=acmecorp then route -> redwood-v1-small. That preserves correctness while reducing KV pressure.

Ben (Infra): I'll also add a short-lived autoscale bump for redwood-v1 GPU pool (add 4 nodes) while we stabilize. That buys time but isn't a long-term fix.

Carla (Support): Noted — telling AcmeCorp we have mitigation plan: circuit breaker + fallback model + autoscale. They asked for ETA.

Alice (SRE): ETA: circuit breaker + fallback in 10–12 mins, autoscale immediate (couple minutes), rollback pin requires approval but we can start canary rollback immediately.

Marc (DevOps): Applying circuit breaker rule now: command:
```
# internal admin API
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/redwood/circuit-breakers -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"tenant":"acmecorp","model":"redwood-v1","concurrency_limit":4,"rate_limit_rps":10,"fail_open":false}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by marc for circuit-breaker-rule/acmecorp (deployment id cb-2026-03-10-0912)

Marc (DevOps): Circuit breaker applied. Observability shows reduced queued requests for acmecorp immediately.

Ben (Infra): Routing rule applied to send acmecorp -> redwood-v1-small.

sre-oncall-bot: autoscale triggered: +4 nodes to pool redwood-v1-gpu-pool, expected ready ~2m.

Alice (SRE): After these changes do we see p99 coming down for acmecorp?

Ben (Infra): Preliminary: p99 reduced from ~3.8s -> ~650ms for that tenant. Global p99 still elevated (1.1s) but trending down.

Carla (Support): AcmeCorp confirmed improvement. They saw fewer timeouts and accept the fallback for now. :thumbsup:

Lisa (Product): Good. Next steps: full root cause: why KV evictions spiked. Was it model rollout behavior, increased prompt size, or a change in cache sizing?

Alice (SRE): Agreed. Postmortem checklist:
- capture exact model commit diff for v2026-03-09-2
- compare memory allocation and KV cache size heuristics
- replay workload in staging with similar concurrency and prompt distribution
- add unit/regression test for KV eviction hot-path
- update SLO guardrails (see below)

Alice (SRE): Proposed SLO guardrails and mitigation playbook (short):
1) Per-tenant soft rate limits: default 20 rps, burst 2x, overridable by contract.
2) Circuit breakers: per-tenant concurrency + error-based tripping (5xx spike or queue_latency > 1s for 5% of requests). Auto-failover to fallback_model or lower-quality variant.
3) Fallback routing: model_variant_order: [redwood-v1, redwood-v1-small, redwood-v1-tiny] with region-aware fallback before cross-region.
4) Autoscale bump as emergency — limited to N minutes then auto-evaluate.
5) Canary gating on model rollouts with KV-eviction synthetic workload.

Marc (DevOps): Add operational runbook step: auto-insert temporary token cap (max_tokens_per_request=2048) when token-cost anomalies detected.

Ben (Infra): Also add a metric alert: kv_cache_evictions_rate > X for 5m triggers SRE page with playbook link.

Carla (Support): I'll update the customer with the postmortem plan and timeline.

Lisa (Product): Let's decide long-term: if v2026-03-09-2 is root cause, we should revert the rollout and add more pre-release evaluation for cache behavior.

Alice (SRE): For action items now (owners):
- Marc: confirm circuit breaker + routing changes are stable; rollback if negative impacts (owner: Marc)
- Ben: run regression test on v2026-03-09-2 in staging with synthetic cache-churn load (owner: Ben)
- Alice: draft postmortem and SLO update (owner: Alice)
- Carla: customer comms + confirm they can resume normal traffic when we sign off (owner: Carla)

Ben (Infra): Running a staged replay now. If reproduces, we'll do a controlled rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback candidate prepared: redwood-v1@v2026-03-09-1 -> ready for canary revert

Alice (SRE): Good. Note for runbook wording: keep mitigations in this order — circuit-breaker, fallback routing, token caps, autoscale, rollback. That preserves availability while minimizing cost.

Marc (DevOps): I'll follow up with a small config diff to make circuit-breaker rules templated so support can enable them per-tenant quickly.

Carla (Support): Customer happy for now, says they'll hold off heavy batch tests until we confirm stability. Closing escalation if metrics stay stable for 30m.

Alice (SRE): Marking thread for postmortem. Closing in 30m if p99 stays within SLOs. Thanks everyone.
